title: Concurrent keychain saves can lose or reject the final value
reasoning: The service advertises Sendable and can be called from concurrent tasks, but save is implemented as delete-then-add. Two concurrent saves for the same key can interleave as delete/delete/add/add, causing one caller to fail with errSecDuplicateItem, or delete/add/delete/add, temporarily removing the secret and making readers observe nil. This is a real race at the API boundary because no actor, lock, or atomic SecItemUpdate/add fallback protects the compound operation.
reproduction: Run two concurrent tasks that call KeychainService.save different values for the same key while a third task retrieves the key; depending on interleaving, one save can throw unableToSave(errSecDuplicateItem) or a retrieve can observe nil between delete and add.
recommendation: Make save atomic: try SecItemAdd first, and on errSecDuplicateItem call SecItemUpdate without deleting; or serialize all operations behind an actor/lock. Do not ignore delete errors during a write path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included DigestGeneratorTests exercise only digest filename generation and EPUB output. There are no KeychainService tests, and no test performs concurrent same-key writes or read-during-write behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a KeychainService concurrency test using a unique serviceName/key that launches many concurrent save calls for the same key, asserts no duplicate-item errors escape, and verifies the final value is one of the written values and never nil after successful completion.
minimumFixScope: Update KeychainService.save(_:forKey:) to use add-or-update semantics atomically, and add focused tests for same-key concurrent writes.
